Title: Users can’t see free/busy information in cross-tenant Outlook calendars using Outlook desktop and Outlook on the web 

User impact: Users can’t see free/busy information in cross-tenant Outlook calendars using Outlook desktop and Outlook on the web.

Current status: We've identified that a recent change introduced a regression that caused cross-tenant mailbox requests to be rejected when a tenant ID was used instead of the mailbox's SMTP address, resulting in impact. We're reverting the change to restore the correct configuration and expect to confirm the deployment timeline by our next scheduled update.

Scope of impact: Your organization is affected by this event, and any user attempting to view free/busy information in cross-tenant Outlook calendars is impacted. This section may be updated as our investigation continues.

Root cause: A recent change introduced a regression that caused cross-tenant mailbox requests to be rejected when a tenant ID was used instead of the mailbox's SMTP address.

Title: Some users may not see free/busy info shared between organizations using cross-tenant access policy in Exchange Online

User impact: Users may not see free/busy info shared between organizations using cross-tenant access policy in Exchange Online.

More info: To remediate impact while our investigation is ongoing, admins can configure free/busy sharing between impacted organizations using Organization Relationship. The Organization Relationship will take precedence over the cross-tenant access policy and sharing will begin working again after caches clear, usually within 2 hours. If EWS has been disabled in your tenant, it will need to be re-enabled to support Organization Relationship. The Organization Relationship should be removed when this incident is resolved.

More information on this process can be viewed here: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/sharing/organization-relationships/create-an-organization-relationship

Current status: After further analysis, we've isolated that additional organizations utilizing cross-tenant access policies are affected by this free/busy issue, and we've expanded communications to all potentially affected users. We've updated the "Title", "User impact", and "Scope of impact" fields of our communications to reflect this. We've initiated deployment of a fix to address a regression introduced by a recent service change that caused cross-tenant mailbox requests to be rejected when a tenant ID was used instead of the mailbox's SMTP address. We're evaluating ways to expedite our deployment and we aim to provide a timeline to remediation as soon as possible

Scope of impact: This issue impacts some users whose organization utilizes cross-tenant access policy, who may be unable to view free/busy info shared between organizations in Exchange Online. This section may be updated as the investigation progresses.

Start time: Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 4:00 PM UTC

Root cause: A recent change introduced a regression that causes cross-tenant mailbox requests to be rejected when a tenant ID was used instead of the mailbox's SMTP address.

Title: Some users may not see free/busy info shared between organizations using cross-tenant access policy in Exchange Online

More info: To remediate impact while our investigation is ongoing, admins can configure free/busy sharing between impacted organizations using Organization Relationship. The Organization Relationship will take precedence over the cross-tenant access policy and sharing will begin working again after caches clear, usually within 2 hours. If EWS has been disabled in your tenant, it will need to be re-enabled to support Organization Relationship. The Organization Relationship should be removed when this incident is resolved.
